_comment: Layer-2 levers — the public-facing 'why isn't X a column?' explainer. Levers are policy INSTRUMENTS parties use to move the fundamentals; we judge them by their EFFECT on the fundamentals, not as outcomes of their own. NOTE (v2, 2026-06-16): economy, tax and immigration were REMOVED as levers — they are now first-class (O13 Prosperity, O11 Tax, and the D1 Immigration direction-only measure). Only genuine instruments remain here. 'affects' references outcome IDs in config/outcomes.json.
principle: We organise around the outcomes you actually feel in your life. A few policy areas — like energy, childcare, or transport — are mainly the tools parties use to move those outcomes, so rather than giving each its own column, we judge each party's use of them by their effect here. That's a deliberate choice, and you're free to disagree with it.
lens_note: Fairness runs through everything. As well as the dedicated 'Inequality & fair shares' column, every single verdict is also examined from a who-gains-who-pays angle, alongside cost, efficiency and deliverability.

levers.name: Energy policy
levers.why: Energy policy is the instrument; what you feel is your bill and the air and climate around you. We score those.

levers.name: Childcare
levers.why: Childcare cost and availability shape what families can afford and whether parents can work — so it shows up inside those outcomes.

levers.name: Transport
levers.why: Transport cost and access are means to a budget that works and getting to a job — we trace them into those outcomes.
